source.title: Block-Cyclic Stochastic Coordinate Descent for Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Kensuke Nakamura; Stefano Soatto; Byung-Woo Hong

record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out image-classification accuracy, using the same training setup; this bears on V4 but is not a direct replication of the cited optimizer studies.
record.gate_note: The study reports adaptive-optimizer comparisons in Table 3. Other results compare BCSC with SGD or report BCSC's robustness to outliers and dropout; those do not test the listed claim versions. Results cited from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Table 3 directly compares AdaGrad and AdaDelta with SGD on held-out CIFAR-10 accuracy, testing V4 under shared customary hyperparameters. Table 2 also tests V6 by varying dropout within each optimizer on MNIST; the record overlooks these comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that BCSC improves accuracy, stability, convergence speed and robustness to training outliers across their tested models, and can work with adaptive learning rates and dropout. They acknowledge added computational cost and leave hyperparameter tuning for future work. They do not draw a general conclusion about adaptive optimizers versus SGD.
record.recipe_differences: BCSC is a different optimizer; for the V4 comparison, AdaGrad and AdaDelta are compared with SGD using customary shared hyperparameters and a manual learning-rate schedule. Hyperparameter search breadth is not stated.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer and epoch segment change the relative test accuracy; the ordering also differs by model.

fits_no_version.finding: BCSC improves accuracy, convergence and robustness to partially corrupted training labels relative to the tested optimization baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Using different mini-batches to update different parameter blocks can improve optimization and robustness to training outliers.

record.problems: The adaptive-optimizer comparison is limited to three Cifar10 models and AdaGrad/AdaDelta; tuning breadth is not reported. Table 3 reports test accuracy but no uncertainty, and the paper does not give a direct training-versus-test gap comparison for these methods.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Table 3 provides the adaptive optimizer and SGD test-accuracy values for all three listed models and four epoch segments.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization; partial label corruption does not establish this.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adam, language benchmarks, optimizer-specific tuning searches, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and whether adaptive methods have equal or better training performance.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Very small training sets, excessive dropout causing underfitting, fully connected classifiers, and removing dropout together with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with other generalization measures.
Removing examples selected by memorization influence versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Within-optimizer dropout comparisons on MNIST LeNet4: at dropout 0/5/10/15%, mean test accuracy is 98.98/99.04/99.09/99.04 for SGD, 99.00/99.10/99.14/99.13 for BCSC M=2, 99.04/99.10/99.17/99.16 for M=4, and 99.02/99.13/99.17/99.19 for M=8. Add comparisons against each configuration's own zero-dropout baseline; all gains are small and uncertainty is unreported.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted Table 3 values match the supplied text. First-half, last-half and all-epoch values summarize accuracy over training rather than final trained-model accuracy. The shared recipe uses 200 epochs, batch size 128, momentum 0.9, weight decay 0.0005 and a prescribed learning-rate schedule; optimizer-specific tuning is not demonstrated. No uncertainty is supplied. The record's later-epoch 'challenges' verdict has its direction wrong: lower adaptive-method accuracy supports V4. Table 2's dropout manipulation tests V6 even though the authors emphasize BCSC's compatibility with dropout.

versions.untested_parts: Language benchmarks, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models.
